speaker: Doctor
text: I am Dr. Agent. I see you are experiencing progressive difficulty walking, urinary incontinence, and speech difficulties; to begin my assessment, have these symptoms been present for months or years, and do you notice any limb stiffness or muscle spasms?

speaker: Patient
text: 54-year-old male. The patient has been experiencing a gradual difficulty in walking over the past 3 months, requiring wheelchair assistance for the last month. Additionally, there is a history of urinary incontinence for 1 year and recent onset of speech slurring making communication challenging.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Amyotrophic Lateral Sclerosis (ALS).

The clinical presentation of progressive quadriparesis requiring wheelchair assistance within three months, combined with long-standing urinary incontinence and recent bulbar symptoms (speech slurring), is highly characteristic of ALS, particularly given the rapid progression of motor deficits. The urinary incontinence likely represents sphincter dysfunction secondary to advanced spinal cord involvement rather than primary neurogenic bladder.
